{{Short description|none}}
The Argentina football champion is the winner of the highest league in Argentine football, the [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]]. The league season have had different formats, since the original [[round-robin tournament|double round-robin]] until the ''Liga Profesional''. The champion is the team with the most points at the end of the competition.

The first Argentine football champions, [[St. Andrew's Athletic Club|St. Andrew's]] and [[Old Caledonians Football Club|Old Caledonians]], were crowned in [[1891 Argentine Primera División|1891]] in the first official championship. [[Alumni Athletic Club|Alumni]] was the most successful club with 10 titles until its dissolution in 1911. [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] is the most successful club, having won 38 titles to date.

==Primera División champions (1891–present)==
The following is a list including all the Primera División champions since the first edition held in 1891.<ref name=afa>{{cite web |title=Campeones de Primera División |url=https://www.afa.com.ar/es/pages/campeones-de-primera-division |publisher=[[Argentine Football Association|AFA]] |access-date=15 April 2020 |language=es}}</ref><ref name=rsf>{{cite web |last1=Osvaldo José Gorgazzi and Héctor Villa Martínez |title=Argentina - List of Champions and Runners-Up |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/argchamp.html |access-date=15 April 2020 |website=[[RSSSF]] |date=12 March 2020}}</ref><ref>''38 Campeones del Fútbol Argentino 1891-2013'' by Diego Estévez, Ediciones Continente - {{ISBN|978-950-754-369-2}}</ref> For the first time since 1892, no league championship was held in 2020 after the schedule for a regular league season had been repeatedly delayed because of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina|COVID-19 pandemic]]. As the [[Government of Argentina|National Government]] allowed football competitions to return in October,<ref>[https://www.ambito.com/deportes/futbol/el-gobierno-dio-via-libre-la-vuelta-del-n5138431 El Gobierno dio vía libre para la vuelta del fútbol] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201105011307/https://www.ambito.com/deportes/futbol/el-gobierno-dio-via-libre-la-vuelta-del-n5138431 |date=2020-11-05 }} on Ámbito.com, 6 Oct 2020</ref> AFA organised the [[2020 Copa de la Liga Profesional]], a [[list of Argentine football national cups|domestic cup]] conceived as a contingency competition.

| rowspan=3 | 45 || [[1936 Argentine Primera División|1936 <small>(H)</small>]] {{refn|The 1936 season was divided into two single [[round-robin tournament]]s, "Copa Campeonato" (won by River Plate) and "Copa de Honor" (won by San Lorenzo). At the end of the season, both teams played the "Copa de Oro", a single match won by River. In its ''Memoria y Balance'' (Annual Report) published by the AFA that year, River Plate is mentioned as "1936 Champion" while San Lorenzo is only mentioned as "Copa de honor winning team".<ref name=memoria36/> In its 100th anniversary book published in 1993, the AFA listed River Plate as the only 1936 champion.<ref>''100 Años con el Fútbol'' (hardcover edition) - Argentine Football Association</ref> In 2013, the AFA included three 1936 championships on its website, mentioning River Plate as Copa de Oro and Copa Campeonato winner and San Lorenzo as Copa de Honor winner, therefore both clubs were added one league title to their honours.<ref>[http://www.clarin.com/deportes/AFA-reconocio-San-Lorenzo-River_0_950905061.html La AFA les reconoció otro título a San Lorenzo y a River] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303231546/http://www.clarin.com/deportes/AFA-reconocio-San-Lorenzo-River_0_950905061.html |date=2016-03-03 }}, ''Clarín'', 6 July 2013</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131216002759/http://cronica.com.ar/diario/2013/07/05/50257-san-lorenzo-y-river-campeones.html 77 años después: San Lorenzo y River, campeones!] on ''Crónica'', 5 July 2013]</ref> Moreover, some historians consider Copa de Oro a national cup instead of a league championship, stating that it was only contested to qualify an Argentine representative to play the [[Copa Aldao]] against the Uruguayan champion.<ref name="barnade"/>|group=note1|name=1936controv}} || [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] {{small|(5)}} || [[Club Atlético Huracán|Huracán]] || [[Boca Juniors]]

| [[2025 AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol#Aggregate table|2025 Liga]] || [[Rosario Central]] {{small|(5)}} {{refn|The AFA awarded Rosario Central a league title due to having earned the most points in the entire season (2025 aggregate table).<ref>[Insólito: la AFA le entregó el trofeo de “Campeón de Liga” a Rosario Central por ser el equipo que más puntos sumó en la Tabla Anual Insólito: la AFA le entregó el trofeo de “Campeón de Liga” a Rosario Central por ser el equipo que más puntos sumó en la Tabla Anual] on infobae.com, 20 Nov 2025</ref> The decision to award the “Campeón de Liga” title to Rosario Central caused wide controversy as the trophy was not announced before the end of the Clausura regular season.<ref>[https://www.latimes.com/espanol/deportes/articulo/2025-11-21/argentina-otorga-titulo-inesperado-y-polemico-de-campeon-de-liga-rosario-central Argentina otorga título inesperado y polémico] at ''Los Angeles Times''. 21 Nov 2025</ref><ref>[https://www.perfil.com/noticias/deportes/el-polemico-titulo-de-rosario-central-una-nueva-mancha-para-la-afa.phtml El polémico título de Rosario Central: una nueva mancha para la AFA] by Román Iucht on Perfil.com, 21 Nov 2025</ref><ref>[https://tn.com.ar/deportes/futbol/2025/11/20/la-decision-de-la-afa-por-que-rosario-central-es-campeon-de-la-liga-2025/ La polémica decisión de la AFA: por qué Rosario Central es campeón de la Liga 2025] on TN. 20 Nov 2025</ref> As the 2025 Tournament Rules stated that changes could be made (prior approval by the Executive Committee) with the season in progress<ref name=reglam25>[https://www.ligaprofesional.ar/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Reglamento-de-Torneos-LPF-2025.pdf ''Reglamento de la Temporada 2025'' - AFA], p. 4</ref> president Claudio Tapia presented an initiative to award a league title to Rosario Central, which was approved and carried out by the committee in November.<ref>[https://assets1.afa.com.ar/2025/Boletines/Boletin-Resoluciones-6794-(20-11-2025).pdf ''Boletin Oficial AFA – Resoluciones 6794 (20-11-2025)'']</ref> The title was established with retroactivity since this 2025 season and will also be disputed in the future seasons.<ref>https://www.lacapital.com.ar/ovacion/la-increible-y-polemica-cantidad-titulos-que-la-afa-pondra-juego-2026-el-futbol-argentino-n10236891.html Diario La Capital de Rosario, 25 de diciembre de 2025. ''La increíble y polémica cantidad de títulos que la AFA pondrá en juego en 2026 en el fútbol argentino.''</ref> |group=note2|name=central5ta}} || [[Boca Juniors]]  || [[Argentinos Juniors]]

== Titles by club ==
<!-- NOTE TO EDITORS: despite of some recent media news, the Argentine Association defines Copa de la Liga Profesional as a "national/domestic cup" (see source: https://www.afa.com.ar/es/pages/campeones-de-primera-division) NOT awarding a league title to past winners. Therefore Boca Juniors still have 35 league titles. Moreover, AFA Bulletin #6405 (https://www.afa.com.ar/upload/torneo/Placas%20categor%C3%ADas/2023/Diciembre/Bolet%C3%ADn%20Comit%C3%A9%20Ejecutivo%206405%20(19-12-2023).pdf) officially proclaimed River Plate as "2023 Primera División champion" and Rosario Central "2023 Copa LPF champion", with no mention of changes at all. -->
The list include all the titles won by each club since the first Primera División championship held in 1891. Clubs in ''italic'' no longer exist or are currently disaffiliated from the AFA.

== Championships defined by tiebreaker matches ==
<!-- NOTE TO EDITORS: this section is *only* for tiebreaker matches after two (or more) teams finished equalled on points at the end of a season. Please don't add finals that were stipulated on the championship rules (p.e. [[Nacional championship]]s, or 2025 Primera División)
-->
Although most of Primera División championships were decided by points in single and double [[round-robin tournament]]s, some [[tiebreaker]] matches were played when two (or more) teams ended tied on points at the end of the season in order to define a champion. The following is a list of those cases:<ref>[http://abrilacancha.com.ar/2021/09/14/un-repaso-unico-las-33-finales-del-futbol-argentino-de-primera-division-hasta-2021/ Un repaso único: las 33 finales del fútbol argentino de Primera División hasta 2021] by Carlos Aira on Abrí La Cancha, 14 Sep 2021</ref>

{{refbegin}}
'''''Notes''''':
# The 1936 "Copa de Oro" is not listed because it did not define a Primera División champion but which team would participate in the [[1936 Copa Aldao]].{{refn|This point is still under discussion and has caused controversies among football historians, as River Plate was mentioned as "Argentine champion" on the AFA Annual Report of that year.<ref name=memoria36>[http://biblioteca.afa.org.ar/libros/libro_13/ ''Memoria y Balance General 1936'', p. 24] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140624014312/http://biblioteca.afa.org.ar/libros/libro_13/ |date=2014-06-24 }} on the Argentine Football Association Library
</ref> Nevertheless, some historians argue that the "Copa de Oro" was not a league title but a national cup that determined which team would play the Copa Aldao v the Uruguayan representative.<ref name=barnade>[https://www.clarin.com/deportes/futbol/titulo-80-anos-despues-sigue-generando-controversia_0_BkRS8JdNl.html Un título que 80 años después sigue generando controversia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116035845/https://www.clarin.com/deportes/futbol/titulo-80-anos-despues-sigue-generando-controversia_0_BkRS8JdNl.html |date=2020-11-16 }} by Oscar Barnade on Clarín, 21 Dec 2016</ref>|group=note3|name=controv}}
# [[Nacional championship|Nacional]] championship finals are listed on their respective articles and not included here. It is due to finals included in the list below were played in exceptional cases (mostly when both teams finished tied on points).
# [[Copa Campeonato]] matches are not included because they had the format of [[list of Argentine football national cups|national cup]].
{{refend}}
